modern: The universal cause is like a winter torrent: it carries everything along with it. But how worthless are all these poor people who are engaged in political matters and, as they suppose, are playing the philosopher! All drivellers. Well then, man: do what nature now requires. Set yourself in motion, if it is in your power, and do not look about you to see if anyone will notice it; nor expect Plato’s Republic: but be content if the smallest thing goes well, and consider such an outcome no small matter. For who can change men’s opinions? And without a change of opinions, what else is there but the slavery of men who groan while they pretend to obey? Come now and tell me of Alexander and Philippus and Demetrius of Phalerum. They themselves shall judge whether they discovered what the common nature required, and trained themselves accordingly. But if they acted like tragic heroes, no one has condemned me to imitate them. Simple and modest is the work of philosophy. Do not draw me aside into insolence and pride.

explained.summary:
The universe sweeps everything along like a flooded river. Marcus is scornful of politicians who think they’re doing philosophy. His own advice is to do what’s needed now, without looking round for an audience, and without waiting for a perfect society like the one in Plato’s Republic. Be glad if even a small thing goes well.

You can’t force people to change their minds, and without that you only get grudging obedience. Alexander the Great, his father Philip and the Athenian statesman Demetrius of Phalerum must answer for whether they truly served the common good. If they were just playing the hero, Marcus doesn’t have to copy them. Philosophy’s work is simple and modest.
explained.today: Think of wanting to fix your whole workplace, family or town at once and feeling defeated when it doesn’t happen. A better aim is to do the next useful thing well, without posting about it, and count a small improvement as a real win.
